concerns.text: The primary target PC_raw is defined as unit‑cell volume divided by the sum of atomic van der Waals volumes (FR‑003). This target is a deterministic function of the molecule’s atomic composition, which is fully encoded in the SMILES string. Even though explicit atom‑count features are excluded from the predictor set, the SMILES embedding inevitably contains composition information, making the prediction task circular/tautological. The plan’s own “Risk Mitigation” bullet admits this but proceeds to evaluate predictive performance, which may simply reflect the trivial composition‑target relationship rather than any genuine topology‑derived signal.

Variance‑inflation‑factor (VIF) diagnostics are applied to *all* predictor variables, including the high‑dimensional SMILES‑Transformer fingerprint vector. VIF assumes a linear regression context with a modest number of predictors; applying it to hundreds of correlated embedding dimensions is statistically inappropriate and can produce misleading collinearity flags.

concerns.location: research.md:Target redefined to PC_raw (FR‑003) vs spec.md:FR‑003 definition
concerns.text: The research document defines PC_raw as unit‑cell volume / ∑V_vdw, whereas the specification (FR‑003) defines the Packing Coefficient as ∑V_vdw / unit‑cell volume. This inconsistency means the target variable used in training/evaluation may be the inverse of the intended metric, leading to contradictory interpretations of correlation signs and magnitude.
